title: Supramolecular network-engineered transparent conductive cellulose/gelatin bioplastics for efficient Joule heating and electromagnetic interference shielding
authors: Wen Gong; Jianyu Zhou; Yuchen Tian; Qi Zhang; Puyan Huang; Run Gan; Xiang He; Miao Miao; Xin Feng
affiliations: ; ; Shanghai University; Shanghai University; Shanghai University; Shanghai Ocean University; Shanghai University; Shanghai University
abstract: Abstract Petroleum-based plastics are indispensable in modern society, yet their non-degradable nature and toxic byproducts have led to severe environmental pollution and ecological threats. The development of bioplastics that combine high optical transparency, excellent tensile strength, and recyclability remains a significant challenge on the path toward sustainability. To address this challenge, a flexible, transparent bioplastic with exceptional mechanical performance, exhibiting a tensile strength of 77.61 MPa and a Young’s modulus of 2022.02 MPa, was prepared via a straightforward self-assembly strategy using gelatin, 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine-1-oxyl (TEMPO)-oxidized cellulose nanofibril and hyaluronic acid, and as raw materials, based on a supramolecular network formed through multiple hydrogen bonding. Based on this, a dense double conductive layer was fabricated on the bioplastic surface via spin-coating of silver nanowires (AgNWs) and subsequent magnetron sputtering of indium tin oxide (ITO), which imparted high electrical conductivity (455.4 S·m−1), outstanding electromagnetic interference shielding (24.26 dB), and efficient electrothermal heating performance. More importantly, the ITO-assisted welding effect on the AgNWs networks enhanced electrical conductivity, interfacial adhesion, bending durability, and long-term environmental stability. With these integrated functionalities, the conductive bioplastic emerges as a sustainable enabler for next-generation flexible electronics and personal thermotherapy.

title: Systematic Optimization of Sputtered AZO Thin Films and Their Integration as Alternative Transparent Electrodes for Perovskite Solar Cells
authors: Zeynep Mavili; Mücahit Yılmaz
affiliations: Necmettin Erbakan University; Necmettin Erbakan University
abstract: Abstract Transparent conducting oxides (TCOs) are critical components of perovskite solar cells (PSCs), motivating the search for low-cost and scalable alternatives to conventional fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO). Among the proposed alternatives, Al-doped ZnO (AZO) has been widely investigated as a low-cost, indium-free transparent conductive oxide. However, systematic studies correlating sputtering parameters with AZO thin film properties and PSC performance through direct benchmarking against commercial FTO under identical device fabrication conditions remain limited. In this study, AZO thin films were systematically optimized by magnetron sputtering through controlled variation of sputtering power, annealing conditions, substrate temperature, and deposition duration. The optimized high-temperature-grown AZO film (AZO-13) exhibited high visible transparency (∼86%), low sheet resistance (1.26 × 101 Ω·sq–1), strong preferential (002) orientation, and high calculated electrical conductivity (∼9.85 × 102 S·cm–1), achieving a Haacke figure of merit (0.668) that slightly surpassed that of commercial FTO (0.664). To evaluate its applicability as a transparent electrode, the optimized AZO film was directly integrated into PSC devices and compared with commercial FTO under identical fabrication conditions. The AZO-based PSC achieved a stabilized efficiency of 16.49%, while comparative PL/TRPL, EQE, and EIS analyses revealed that the lower device performance mainly originated from increased interfacial resistance and less efficient charge extraction. In addition, AZO exhibited improved long-wavelength transparency compared with FTO, suggesting potential relevance for tandem-oriented photovoltaic applications. These results establish a clear process–structure–property–device relationship for sputtered AZO thin films and demonstrate their potential as alternative TCO electrodes for PSC technologies.
keywords: Al-doped ZnO; transparent conducting oxides; perovskite solar cells; sputtering process optimization; sheet resistance; (002) preferred orientation; interfacial resistance; charge extraction

title: Tailoring the properties of Er-doped IZO thin films via controlled RF magnetron co-sputtering for photovoltaic applications
authors: Mohsin Khan; Qasim Ali; Rashid Ali; Muhammad Bilal Asif; Ghazi Aman Nowsherwan; Mahrukh Shafeeq; Saira Riaz; Mansun Chan; Shahzad Naseem
affiliations: University of the Punjab | Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; University of the Punjab; Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences and Technology; Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; University of the Punjab; University of the Punjab; University of the Punjab; Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; University of the Punjab
abstract: Abstract Er-doped indium zinc oxide (Er–IZO) thin films were deposited on glass substrates via radio-frequency magnetron co-sputtering, maintaining 90 W RF power on the IZO target while varying the Er DC power at 20, 30, and 40 W. XRD analysis showed that moderate Er incorporation (30 W) produced the largest crystallite size (31.76 nm), whereas excessive doping (40 W) reduced the coherence length to 28.40 nm due to increased lattice distortion. UV-VIS spectroscopy confirmed > 80% visible transparency for all samples, with the optical bandgap increasing from 3.28 eV (pristine) to 3.43 eV (20 W) and 3.80 eV (30 W) via the Burstein–Moss effect. A slight bandgap reduction to 3.50 eV at 40 W is attributed to defect-induced carrier compensation and enhanced scattering, which also caused minor transmission losses. Photoelectron spectroscopy revealed a non-monotonic work-function evolution: an initial decrease from 4.18 to 3.92 eV at 20 W, a modest increase to 3.94 eV at 30 W, and a larger rise to 4.32 eV at 40 W, driven by dopant clustering, carrier trapping, and electronic-structure modification. These results highlight the delicate balance between dopant incorporation, lattice integrity, and electronic behavior that governs the optimization of Er-doped IZO thin films as photovoltaic-relevant transparent conducting and optoelectronic materials.

title: The Preparation and Optoelectronic Properties of Symmetric and Asymmetric Multilayered Transparent Conductive Films with ZnS-TiO2-Ag Material System
authors: Kai Tao; Hanbin Chen; Fangzi Zhao; Shiqi Li; Zhiyong Liu
affiliations: Henan Institute of Technology; Southwest Technology and Engineering Research Institute (China); Henan Institute of Technology; Henan Institute of Technology; University of Science and Technology Beijing
abstract: Flexible transparent conductive films with symmetric and asymmetric multilayered structures are studied using the ZnS–TiO2–Ag material system, in order to capitalize on the divergent properties of the two dielectric layers for improved performance. The dielectric/metal/dielectric-structured films were deposited by magnetron sputtering sequentially, with high-purity targets. Multilayered films with various dielectric combinations and metallic layer thicknesses were prepared and analyzed. The surface morphology and phase structure were characterized by atomic force microscopy and scanning electronic microscopy. The optical properties were tested by spectrophotometry and analyzed by numerical simulation approach. The sheet resistance was measured via a four-point probe tester. Among the series of multilayers, asymmetric ZnS/Ag/TiO2 film with 35 nm thickness of dielectric layers and 8.5 nm of metallic layer possesses the optimum comprehensive optoelectronic performance. The average light transmittance reaches 90.72% in the visible spectrum, and the sheet resistance is 7.69 Ω/sq. The good result is ascribed primarily to the combined advantages of superior percolation effect of bottom ZnS layer on ultrathin Ag layer, beneficial impingement effect of top layer deposition on the metallic layer, and excellent surface smoothness of the top dielectric layer.
keywords: transparent conductive films; multilayer films; flexible electronics; sheet resistance; optical transmittance; percolation effect; dielectric-metal-dielectric structure; optoelectronic properties; surface morphology
